one_sentence: The swing towards Northgate came from two close-range chances in minutes 52 and 53, one of which Joss Sorel scored, after Harbour City's earlier shooting dried up; nothing in the data shows a change in either team's players, shape or substitutions that caused it.
evidence: xG (A minus B) went from -0.31 in minutes 40-51 to +0.30 in minutes 52-60, a swing of 0.61 that is the largest adjacent-window swing of the match, but a team-label permutation test gives p = 0.08
Harbour City's shots fell from 4 (xG 0.49) in minutes 40-51 to 2 (xG 0.09) in minutes 52-60, while their final-third actions held steady (22 before, 19 after)
Northgate's two shots after minute 52 were both high quality (xG 0.195 and 0.197, xG per shot 0.20 vs 0.09 before), while their final-third actions fell from 11 to 9
Team mean x moved by the same amount for both sides (A 38.0 to 36.2, B 61.1 to 59.0), so there is no sign of a tactical change
No substitution before minute 52 (first substitution is minute 63, for Harbour City); the only cards came at minutes 33 and 69
alternatives_ruled_out: Substitution: the first substitution in the match is at minute 63 (B13 for B7) and every change is after the shift onset
Card-driven change: Northgate A4 (yellow, minute 33) increased his activity after the card (9 to 11 events), and the only other card is at minute 69
Team tactical change: mean player position moved by the same -2 m for both teams, and pitch-wide speed patterns are unchanged
General fatigue: every player slows by about 1 km/h from minutes 0-30 to 61-95, and Northgate's Quin Nasser (A10) stayed slow, which would not help the team that gained momentum
Harbour City pressure: under-pressure events fell from 3 of 82 to 0 of 53, too few to explain the swing (not significant)
Player B6 (Xavi Mbeki) fading: his activity dropped the most (11 to 1 events, z = -1.8), but his speed recovers after minute 61 and the drop is not significant after testing 22 players
